bitbybit.jscad.transformSolids_descripti:
Moves, rotates or scales several solids with the same transformation, giving new solids in
the same order.

`transformation` is one 4x4 matrix, a list of matrices applied in order, or a list of such
lists; a flat 2D shape or a path throws an error.
bitbybit.jscad.transformSolid_descriptio:
Moves, rotates or scales a solid with a transformation, giving a new solid.

`transformation` is one 4x4 matrix, a list of matrices applied in order, or a list of such
lists; a flat 2D shape or a path throws an error.
bitbybit.jscad.downloadSolidSTL_descript:
Writes a solid as a binary STL file, the common format for 3D printing, and downloads it in
the browser as `fileName` plus `.stl`.
bitbybit.jscad.downloadSolidsSTL_descrip:
Writes several solids into one binary STL file and downloads it in the browser as `fileName`
plus `.stl`.
bitbybit.jscad.downloadGeometryDxf_descr:
Writes a solid, a 2D shape, a path or a list of them as a DXF drawing file and downloads it
in the browser as `fileName` plus `.dxf`.

`options` is passed to the DXF writer as it is and can stay out.
bitbybit.jscad.downloadGeometry3MF_descr:
Writes a solid, a 2D shape, a path or a list of them as a 3MF file, a modern 3D printing
format, and downloads it in the browser as `fileName` plus `.3mf`.

`options` is passed to the 3MF writer as it is and can stay out.
bitbybit.jscad.booleans.intersect_descri:
Keeps only the volume or area that all the inputs share, dropping everything else.

The inputs must all be solids or all be 2D shapes; an empty result is possible when they do
not overlap.
bitbybit.jscad.booleans.subtract_descrip:
Cuts every later input out of the first one, leaving what remains of the first.

The inputs must all be solids or all be 2D shapes; the order matters, the first is the one
being cut.
bitbybit.jscad.booleans.union_descriptio:
Fuses all the inputs into one solid or one 2D shape, merging where they overlap and keeping
separate parts as one entity.

The inputs must all be solids or all be 2D shapes.
bitbybit.jscad.booleans.intersectTwo_des:
Keeps only the volume or area that `first` and `second` share, the two-input form of
`intersect`.
bitbybit.jscad.booleans.subtractTwo_desc: Cuts `second` out of `first`, the two-input form of `subtract`.
bitbybit.jscad.booleans.unionTwo_descrip: Fuses `first` and `second` into one, the two-input form of `union`.
bitbybit.jscad.booleans.subtractFrom_des:
Cuts every entry of `meshes` out of `from`, leaving what remains of `from`; the same as
`subtract` with the base geometry named separately.
bitbybit.jscad.expansions.expand_descrip:
Grows geometry by moving its whole boundary outward by `delta`, or shrinks it when `delta` is
negative.

A 2D shape stays a 2D shape, a path becomes a 2D band of that width around it, and a solid
grows into a bigger solid, with round corners and a positive `delta` only. Corners are
rounded when `corners` is left out.
bitbybit.jscad.expansions.offset_descrip:
Builds the outline of a 2D shape or path at distance `delta` from the original, outward for
positive and inward for negative.

A 2D shape gives a bigger or smaller 2D shape and a path gives a parallel path. When
`corners` is left out, corners are kept sharp.
bitbybit.jscad.extrusions.extrudeLinear_:
Extrudes a flat 2D shape straight along Z by `height` into a solid, twisting it on the way
when `twistAngle` is not zero.

`twistAngle` in degrees turns the top relative to the bottom around Z and `twistSteps` is the
number of slices used for it, at least 1. A negative `height` extrudes downward.
bitbybit.jscad.extrusions.extrudeRectang:
Builds a wall along the outline of a 2D shape or path: the outline is thickened by `size` on
each side and raised by `height` along Z.

The wall stands on the XY plane and is twice `size` thick, centered on the outline; the
inside of a 2D shape stays empty. A list of inputs gives a list of walls.

Builds a wall along a polyline of points, as `extrudeRectangular` does for a path: the line
is thickened by `size` on each side and raised by `height` along Z.

Only the X and Y coordinates of the points are used and repeated consecutive points are
dropped.
bitbybit.jscad.extrusions.extrudeRotate_:
Revolves a flat 2D shape around the Z axis into a solid.

The shape lies in the XY plane, so its X coordinate is its distance from the axis, and a
shape crossing the axis is clipped there. `angle` and `startAngle` are in degrees, 360 makes
a full ring, and `segments` counts the steps of a full turn.
bitbybit.jscad.hulls.hullChain_descripti:
Wraps each consecutive pair of inputs in a convex hull and fuses the hulls, so a row of
shapes becomes a continuous strand that follows their order.

A bend in the row is kept, where `hull` would fill it in. All inputs must be of the same
kind.
bitbybit.jscad.hulls.hull_description:
Wraps all the inputs in one convex hull, the smallest shape without dents that contains them
all, regardless of their order.

All inputs must be of the same kind, solids, 2D shapes or paths.
bitbybit.jscad.path.createFromPoints_des:
Builds a 2D path through the points in order, open or closed back to the first point as
`closed` says.

Only X and Y of each point are used and repeated consecutive points are removed.
bitbybit.jscad.path.createPathsFromPoint:
Builds one 2D path per list of points, in the same order; a list whose last point coincides
with its first becomes a closed path, any other stays open.

Only X and Y of each point are used and repeated consecutive points are removed.
bitbybit.jscad.path.createFromPolyline_d:
Builds a 2D path through the points of a polyline, open or closed back to the first point as
`closed` says, whatever the polyline's own flag holds.

Only X and Y of each point are used and repeated consecutive points are removed.
bitbybit.jscad.path.createEmpty_descript:
Makes an empty open 2D path with no points, a starting point for `appendPoints`,
`appendPolyline` and `appendArc`.
bitbybit.jscad.path.close_description:
Closes an open 2D path by joining its last point back to its first, giving a closed copy; a
path that is already closed comes back closed.

A 2D shape or a solid throws an error.
bitbybit.jscad.path.appendPoints_descrip:
Adds points to the end of an open 2D path, giving a longer copy.

Only X and Y of each point are used and repeated consecutive points are removed; a closed
path throws an error.
bitbybit.jscad.path.appendPolyline_descr:
Adds the points of a polyline to the end of an open 2D path, giving a longer copy.

Only X and Y of each point are used and repeated consecutive points are removed; a closed
path throws an error.
bitbybit.jscad.path.appendArc_descriptio:
Adds an elliptical arc from the last point of an open 2D path to `endPoint`, giving a longer
copy.

`radiusX` and `radiusY` size the ellipse and `xAxisRotation` tilts it in degrees; `clockwise`
and `large` pick one of the four arcs that fit, and radii too small to reach the end point
are scaled up.
bitbybit.jscad.polygon.createFromPoints_:
Builds a filled 2D shape from the outline points, taken in order and closed back to the
first.

Only X and Y are used, Z is dropped; repeated consecutive points are removed and at least
three distinct points are needed. Counter-clockwise order gives a normal shape, clockwise
gives a negative one.
bitbybit.jscad.polygon.createFromPolylin:
Builds a filled 2D shape from the points of a polyline, closed back to the first point
whatever the polyline says.

Only X and Y are used, Z is dropped; repeated consecutive points are removed and at least
three distinct points are needed.
bitbybit.jscad.polygon.createFromCurve_d:
Builds a filled 2D shape from a NURBS curve by sampling it into points and closing the
outline.

Only X and Y of the sampled points are used, Z is dropped.
bitbybit.jscad.polygon.createFromPath_de:
Builds a filled 2D shape from the points of a 2D path, closed back to the first point.

Repeated consecutive points are removed and at least three distinct points are needed; a 2D
shape or a solid throws an error.
bitbybit.jscad.polygon.circle_descriptio:
Builds a filled circle of the given `radius` around a 2D `center`; `segments` is the number
of straight sides that approximate it.
bitbybit.jscad.polygon.ellipse_descripti:
Builds a filled ellipse around a 2D `center`, with `radius` holding the X and Y half-sizes;
`segments` is the number of straight sides that approximate it.
bitbybit.jscad.polygon.rectangle_descrip: Builds a filled rectangle around a 2D `center`, with `width` along X and `length` along Y.
bitbybit.jscad.polygon.roundedRectangle_:
Builds a filled rectangle with its four corners rounded by `roundRadius`, around a 2D
`center` with `width` along X and `length` along Y.

`roundRadius` must be less than half of the smaller side or an error is thrown; `segments`
sets how smoothly each corner is faceted.
bitbybit.jscad.polygon.square_descriptio:
Builds a filled square of side `size` around a 2D `center`, with its sides parallel to the
axes.
bitbybit.jscad.polygon.star_description:
Builds a filled star with `vertices` tips around a 2D `center`, the tips at `outerRadius` and
the notches between them at `innerRadius`.

`startAngle` in degrees turns the first tip away from the X axis. `density` matters only when
`innerRadius` is 0: the notch radius is then derived from it, as in a pentagram with density
2.
bitbybit.jscad.shapes.cube_description:
Builds a cube of edge length `size` centered on `center`, with its faces parallel to the
axes.
bitbybit.jscad.shapes.cubesOnCenterPoint: Builds one cube of edge length `size` on every point of `centers`, in the same order.
bitbybit.jscad.shapes.cuboid_description:
Builds a box centered on `center` with `width` along X, `height` along Y and `length` along
Z, its faces parallel to the axes.
bitbybit.jscad.shapes.cuboidsOnCenterPoi:
Builds one box of the given `width`, `height` and `length` on every point of `centers`, in
the same order.
bitbybit.jscad.shapes.cylinderElliptic_d:
Builds a cylinder with an elliptical cross-section whose radii can differ at the two ends,
standing along Z and centered on `center`.

`startRadius` is the X and Y radius at the bottom end and `endRadius` at the top, so unequal
pairs make a tapered or cone-like solid; `height` is split evenly above and below `center`.
bitbybit.jscad.shapes.cylinderEllipticOn:
Builds one elliptic cylinder with the given radii and height on every point of `centers`, in
the same order, as `cylinderElliptic` does for one.
bitbybit.jscad.shapes.cylinder_descripti:
Builds a round cylinder of the given `radius` standing along Z, with `height` split evenly
above and below `center`.

`segments` is the number of flat sides around it; more makes it rounder.
bitbybit.jscad.shapes.cylindersOnCenterP:
Builds one cylinder of the given `radius` and `height` on every point of `centers`, in the
same order, as `cylinder` does for one.
bitbybit.jscad.shapes.ellipsoid_descript:
Builds an ellipsoid, a sphere stretched separately along X, Y and Z, centered on `center`.

`radius` holds the three half-sizes in `[x, y, z]` order; equal values make a sphere.
bitbybit.jscad.shapes.ellipsoidsOnCenter:
Builds one ellipsoid with the given radii on every point of `centers`, in the same order, as
`ellipsoid` does for one.
bitbybit.jscad.shapes.geodesicSphere_des:
Builds a sphere from evenly sized triangles, the way a geodesic dome is built, centered on
`center`.

`frequency` is how finely the twenty starting faces are subdivided; it is used in whole
multiples of 6 and must be at least 6, and higher values give a rounder sphere.
bitbybit.jscad.shapes.geodesicSpheresOnC:
Builds one geodesic sphere of the given `radius` on every point of `centers`, in the same
order, as `geodesicSphere` does for one.
bitbybit.jscad.shapes.roundedCuboid_desc:
Builds a box with all its edges and corners rounded by `roundRadius`, centered on `center`
with `width` along X, `height` along Y and `length` along Z.

`roundRadius` must be less than half of the smallest side or an error is thrown; `segments`
sets how smoothly the rounding is faceted.
bitbybit.jscad.shapes.roundedCuboidsOnCe:
Builds one rounded box with the given sides and rounding on every point of `centers`, in the
same order, as `roundedCuboid` does for one.
bitbybit.jscad.shapes.roundedCylinder_de:
Builds a cylinder standing along Z whose two rims are rounded by `roundRadius`, with `height`
split evenly above and below `center`.

`height` must be more than twice `roundRadius` or an error is thrown.
bitbybit.jscad.shapes.roundedCylindersOn:
Builds one rounded cylinder with the given size and rounding on every point of `centers`, in
the same order, as `roundedCylinder` does for one.
bitbybit.jscad.shapes.sphere_description:
Builds a sphere of the given `radius` centered on `center`; `segments` is the number of
facets around it, so more makes it rounder.
bitbybit.jscad.shapes.spheresOnCenterPoi:
Builds one sphere of the given `radius` on every point of `centers`, in the same order, as
`sphere` does for one.
bitbybit.jscad.shapes.torus_description:
Builds a torus, a ring with a round cross-section, lying flat in the XY plane around the
origin with Z through its hole.

`outerRadius` is the distance from the center to the middle of the tube and `innerRadius` the
tube's own radius, which must be smaller. Rotations and `startAngle` are in degrees; an
`outerRotation` below 360 leaves the ring open.
bitbybit.jscad.shapes.fromPolygonPoints_:
Builds a solid from its faces, each given as a list of points that go around the face.

List the points of every face clockwise as seen from outside the solid; the faces must close
the solid for booleans to work on it. The lists are reversed in place while the solid is
built.
bitbybit.jscad.text.cylindricalText_desc:
Writes text as solids: every pen stroke becomes a chain of cylinders standing along Z, hulled
together into one smooth solid, so a letter like A gives several solids.

The strokes lie in the XY plane, centered on the origin, and the cylinders are
`extrusionHeight` long with half above and half below the plane.
bitbybit.jscad.text.sphericalText_descri:
Writes text as solids: every pen stroke becomes a chain of spheres hulled together into one
rounded solid, so a letter like A gives several solids.

The strokes lie in the XY plane, centered on the origin, and the spheres of `radius` sit on
that plane.
bitbybit.jscad.text.createVectorText_des:
Writes text as pen strokes: each stroke is a list of 2D points in the XY plane, and a letter
may take several.

The text starts at `xOffset`, `yOffset` and is not centered; `height` is the height of a
capital letter, `lineSpacing` and `letterSpacing` scale the gaps and `align` places the lines
of a multi-line text.
bitbybit.jscad.colors.colorize_descripti:
Gives a solid, a 2D shape or a path a fixed color from a hex string, returning a colored
copy; a list gives a list of colored copies in the same order.

The color wins over the color of the drawing options, so leave the entity uncolored to
control it there.
bitbybit.manifold.manifoldToMeshPointer_: Turns manifold shape into a mesh pointer that lives in worker's memory. This pointer can be used with bitbybit.manifold.mesh functions
bitbybit.manifold.decomposeManifoldOrCro:
Turns a solid into plain mesh data, or a cross-section into its polygons, ready for drawing
or export.

`normalIdx` names the vertex property channel that holds normals, when the solid carries
them.
bitbybit.manifold.decomposeManifoldsOrCr:
Turns several solids into mesh data, or cross-sections into polygons, as
`decomposeManifoldOrCrossSection` does for one.

`normalIdx` gives one normal channel per shape.
bitbybit.manifold.deleteManifoldOrCrossS:
Frees the memory a solid or a cross-section holds inside the kernel; the object cannot be
used afterwards. Call it for results a script no longer needs, so long sessions do not run
out of memory.
bitbybit.manifold.deleteManifoldsOrCross:
Frees the memory several solids or cross-sections hold inside the kernel; they cannot be used
afterwards. Call it for results a script no longer needs, so long sessions do not run out of
memory.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.manifoldToMes:
Turns a solid into plain mesh data: vertex properties, triangle indexes and the runs that
group triangles by their original shape.

`normalIdx` names the vertex property channel that holds normals, when the solid carries
them.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.manifoldsToMe:
Turns several solids into plain mesh data, as `manifoldToMesh` does for one.

`normalIdx` gives one normal channel per solid.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.shapes.manifo:
Builds a solid from plain mesh data, the form `manifoldToMesh` hands out, so a mesh can make
a round trip through other tools.

The mesh must be closed and consistently oriented, or an error is thrown; degenerate
triangles and unneeded vertices are removed on the way in.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.shapes.cube_d:
Creates a box solid with the given size along X, Y and Z.

With `center` true the box is centered on the origin; otherwise its corner sits on the origin
and it extends along the positive axes.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.shapes.sphere:
Creates a sphere solid of the given radius, centered on the origin.

`circularSegments` is the number of segments around the sphere; it is rounded up to a
multiple of four, since the sphere is built by refining an octahedron.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.shapes.tetrah:
Creates a tetrahedron solid centered on the origin, with one corner at `[1, 1, 1]` and the
others placed symmetrically.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.shapes.cylind:
Creates a cylinder solid standing along Z, or a cone when the top radius differs from the
bottom one.

`radiusLow` is the bottom radius and must be above 0, `radiusHigh` the top radius, which may
be 0 for a point; `circularSegments` sets how round the sides are. `center` centers the
cylinder on the origin instead of standing it on it.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.booleans.subt: Cuts the second solid out of the first, leaving what remains of the first.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.booleans.add_: Fuses two solids into one closed, watertight solid.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.booleans.inte: Keeps only the volume two solids share, dropping everything else.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.booleans.diff: Cuts the second solid out of the first, the same as `subtract`.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.booleans.unio: Fuses two solids into one, the same as `add`.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.booleans.inte: Keeps only the volume two solids share, the same as `intersect`.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.booleans.diff: Cuts every further solid in the list out of the first one.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.booleans.unio: Fuses all the solids in a list into one.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.booleans.inte: Keeps only the volume all the solids in a list share.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.booleans.spli:
Cuts a solid with another solid and keeps both pieces: the part inside the cutter and the
part outside it.

Cheaper than an intersection followed by a subtraction when both are needed.

Cuts a solid with a plane and keeps both pieces.

The plane is given by its normal and its distance from the origin along that normal; the
first piece lies on the side the normal points to, the second on the other side.

Cuts a solid into slabs with several parallel planes, all with the same normal, at the given
distances from the origin.

Each cut keeps the part on the far side of the normal as a finished piece and carries the
rest to the next distance, so the offsets should increase; n offsets give n + 1 pieces, empty
ones dropped.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.booleans.trim:
Cuts a solid with a plane and keeps only the part on the side the normal points to.

The plane is given by its normal and its distance from the origin along that normal.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.operations.hu:
Wraps a solid in its convex hull, the smallest shape without dents that contains it, like
shrink-wrap pulled tight over it.

Wraps points, solids or a mix of both in one convex hull, the smallest shape without dents
that contains them all.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.operations.sl:
Cuts a solid with a plane parallel to the XY plane at the given Z height and returns the flat
section as a cross-section.

A height at the bottom of the solid's bounding box gives its bottom faces; a height at the
top gives an empty cross-section.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.operations.pr:
Flattens a solid onto the XY plane and returns its outline as a cross-section, like its
shadow under a light straight above.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.operations.se:
Gives a solid a new tolerance, the rounding error it is allowed to carry, and simplifies its
mesh when the tolerance grows.

Triangles thinner than the tolerance are treated as degenerate and removed.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.operations.re:
Reserves a run of `count` unique mesh ids and returns the first, for marking sets of
triangles that can be found again after later operations.

Assign them to a mesh's `runOriginalID` before building a solid from it, for instance to keep
several materials apart.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.operations.as:
Makes a copy of a solid that counts as a new original, so the copy can carry its own vertex
properties, such as a different UV mapping, and be told apart from what it was built from.

Coplanar faces are merged and the edges between them collapsed on the way; keep the mesh
route instead when those edges must stay.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.operations.co:
Packs several solids into one without fusing them, the inverse of `decompose`.

Nothing is checked for overlap, so keep the solids apart; a boolean union is the right tool
for overlapping ones.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.operations.de:
Splits a solid into its separate, unconnected pieces, the inverse of `compose`.

A solid that is all one piece comes back as a list of one copy.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.operations.ca:
Computes a normal for every vertex from the mesh and stores it in three property channels
starting at `normalIdx`.

Edges sharper than `minSharpAngle`, in degrees, keep separate normals on each side and stay
crisp; at 0 every triangle keeps its own normal. Flat faces of several triangles stay flat.

Computes how strongly the surface bends at every vertex and stores it in property channels:
Gaussian curvature at `gaussianIdx`, mean curvature at `meanIdx`.

Curvature is the inverse of the bending radius, positive where the surface is convex and
negative where it is concave; an index below 0 skips that channel.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.operations.re:
Adds triangles to a smoothed solid until every point of its mesh lies within `tolerance` of
the smooth surface, so tightly curved regions get more triangles than flat ones.

Only a solid that was smoothed with `smoothOut` or `smoothByNormals` changes; any other comes
back as a copy.

Adds triangles to a solid by splitting every edge into pieces of roughly the given length,
adding inner vertices to keep the triangles even.

On a solid smoothed with `smoothOut` or `smoothByNormals` the new vertices move onto the
smooth surface; otherwise the surface stays as it is.

Adds triangles to a solid by splitting every edge into `number` pieces; with 2, each triangle
becomes four.

On a solid smoothed with `smoothOut` or `smoothByNormals` the new vertices move onto the
smooth surface; otherwise the new triangles stay flat.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.operations.sm:
Marks a solid for smoothing by working out tangents from its triangles, so a later `refine`
or `refineToLength` bends the new triangles into a smooth surface.

Edges sharper than `minSharpAngle`, in degrees, stay sharp; `minSmoothness` above 0 rounds
those a little, and 1 smooths everything. The geometry itself does not change until it is
refined.

Marks a solid for smoothing using the normals stored in its vertex properties, so a later
`refine` or `refineToLength` bends the new triangles into a smooth surface.

`normalIdx` is the first of the three normal channels, as `calculateNormals` stores them;
where the normals on a vertex disagree the edge stays sharp.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.transforms.sc: Scales a solid by a separate factor along X, Y and Z, about the origin.

Scales a solid by a factor per axis, about the origin; it takes the same inputs as `scale3D`,
so use equal factors for a uniform scale.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.transforms.mi:
Mirrors a solid across the plane through the origin with the given normal.

A zero-length normal gives an empty solid.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.transforms.tr: translate
Moves a solid by a vector, in model units.
translate by vectors
Makes one moved copy of a solid per vector, for laying out repeats.
translate xyz
Moves a solid by separate distances along X, Y and Z, in model units.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.transforms.ro:
Rotates a solid about the origin by Euler angles in degrees: first about X, then Y, then Z.

Multiples of 90 degrees are exact, with no rounding error.

Rotates a solid about the origin by separate angles in degrees about X, then Y, then Z.

Multiples of 90 degrees are exact, with no rounding error.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.transforms.tr: transform

Applies a 4x4 matrix to a solid.

The matrix is column-major, 16 numbers with the translation at indexes 12 to 14; the kernel
reads it as a 3x4 affine transform and ignores the last row.
transforms

Applies a list of 4x4 matrices to a solid one after another, first to last, and returns the
final result.

An empty list throws an error.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.evaluate.surf: Measures the total surface area of a solid, in square model units.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.evaluate.volu: Measures the volume of a solid, in cubic model units.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.evaluate.isEm:
Tells whether a solid has no triangles at all, as the result of an intersection of shapes
that do not overlap would.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.evaluate.numV: Counts the vertices of a solid's mesh, the corners its triangles share.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.evaluate.numT: Counts the triangles of a solid's mesh, which is its whole surface.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.evaluate.numE: Counts the edges of a solid's mesh, each shared by two triangles.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.evaluate.numP: Counts the property channels each vertex of a solid carries; the position alone takes three.

Counts the property vertices of a solid, which is at least `numVert`: a vertex whose
neighboring triangles carry different properties, such as a sharp edge with two normals, is
stored more than once.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.evaluate.boun: Finds the axis-aligned box around every vertex of a solid.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.evaluate.tole:
Reads the tolerance of a solid, the rounding error that has built up over the transforms and
operations that made it.

Triangles thinner than this are treated as degenerate and removed.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.evaluate.genu:
Counts the holes through a solid, the way a ring has one and a sphere none.

It only makes sense for a single connected piece, so run `operations.decompose` first on a
solid made of several.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.evaluate.minG:
Measures the smallest distance between two solids, searching no farther than `searchLength`.

The result is between 0 and the search length.
bitbybit.manifold.manifold.evaluate.orig:
Reads the id of a solid that is an original, as `operations.asOriginal` or a freshly built
solid makes it; a solid produced from others by an operation reports -1.
bitbybit.manifold.crossSection.crossSect: cross section to polygons
Reads a cross-section back as its polygons, each a list of 2D points.
cross sections to polygons

Reads several cross-sections back as their polygons, as `crossSectionToPolygons` does for
one.
bitbybit.manifold.crossSection.shapes.cr:
Builds a cross-section from polygons given as 2D points, fusing overlapping ones so the
result has no crossings.

`fillRule` decides which regions count as inside where polygons overlap or a polygon crosses
itself.
bitbybit.manifold.crossSection.shapes.sq:
Creates a square cross-section of the given side; with `center` true it is centered on the
origin, otherwise its corner sits there.
bitbybit.manifold.crossSection.shapes.ci:
Creates a circular cross-section of the given radius, centered on the origin and drawn with
`circularSegments` straight sides.
bitbybit.manifold.crossSection.shapes.re:
Creates a rectangular cross-section with `length` along X and `height` along Y; with `center`
true it is centered on the origin, otherwise its corner sits there.
bitbybit.manifold.crossSection.operation:
Wraps a cross-section in its convex hull, the smallest outline without dents that contains
it, like a rubber band stretched around it.

Sweeps a cross-section along Z into a solid of the given height.

`twistDegrees` turns the top against the bottom, `scaleTopX` and `scaleTopY` shrink or grow
it, and `nDivisions` adds sections in between so twists and tapers stay smooth; 0 for both
top scales makes a cone. `center` centers the solid on the XY plane instead of standing it on
it.

Spins a cross-section around the Y axis into a solid, like a lathe; only the part of the
outline on the positive X side is used.

`revolveDegrees` below 360 gives a partial turn and `circularSegments` sets how round the
result is. The kernel stands the result along Z; `matchProfile`, true by default, turns it
back to match the profile.

Moves the outline of a cross-section outward by `delta`, or inward for a negative delta, so
an outer contour grows and a hole shrinks.

`joinType` says how corners are treated: rounded, squared off, mitered or beveled;
`miterLimit` caps how far a miter may reach and `circularSegments` how round a rounded corner
is. `simplify` afterwards cleans up tiny segments.

Removes points of a cross-section that lie within `epsilon` of the line between their
neighbors, dropping near-duplicates and collinear points.

A larger epsilon removes more; run it after `offset` to clean up the tiny segments offsetting
leaves behind.

Packs several cross-sections or polygons into one cross-section without fusing them, the
inverse of `decompose`.

Splits a cross-section into its separate, unconnected outlines, each with its own holes, the
inverse of `compose`.
Cuts the second cross-section out of the first, leaving what remains of the first.
Fuses two cross-sections into one outline, holes and all.
Keeps only the area two cross-sections share, dropping everything else.
Cuts the second cross-section out of the first, the same as `subtract`.
Fuses two cross-sections into one, the same as `add`.
Keeps only the area two cross-sections share, the same as `intersect`.
Cuts every further cross-section in the list out of the first one.
Fuses all the cross-sections in a list into one.
Keeps only the area all the cross-sections in a list share.
bitbybit.manifold.crossSection.transform: Scales a cross-section by a separate factor along X and Y, about the origin.
Scales a cross-section uniformly about the origin by a factor.

Mirrors a cross-section across the line through the origin that is perpendicular to the given
normal.
Moves a cross-section by a 2D vector, in model units.
Moves a cross-section by separate distances along X and Y, in model units.
Rotates a cross-section about the origin by an angle in degrees, counterclockwise.

Applies a 3x3 matrix to a cross-section, for any combination of move, turn, scale and shear
in the plane.
Measures the area of a cross-section, in square model units, holes excluded.
Tells whether a cross-section has no contours at all.
Counts the vertices of a cross-section over all its contours.
Counts the contours of a cross-section: its outer outlines and its holes.

Finds the rectangle around a cross-section as two 2D points: the minimum corner, then the
maximum corner.
bitbybit.manifold.mesh.operations.merge_:
Fills in the mesh's merge information so it can become a solid again: vertices on open edges
within the tolerance are merged, keeping existing entries.

A mesh that is already closed is left alone and false comes back. Meant for a mesh whose
merge data was lost in a file; the rebuilt solid reports a status if still open.
bitbybit.manifold.mesh.evaluate.position: Reads the position of one vertex of a mesh.
bitbybit.manifold.mesh.evaluate.verts_de: Reads the three vertex indexes of one triangle of a mesh, in counterclockwise order.
bitbybit.manifold.mesh.evaluate.tangent_:
Reads the tangent of one half-edge of a smoothed mesh: the direction the surface leaves the
edge's start vertex in, as three numbers plus a weight.

Half-edge three times the triangle index plus `j` is the edge of triangle `t` that starts at
its `j`-th vertex; a mesh without smoothing tangents has none.
bitbybit.manifold.mesh.evaluate.extras_d:
Reads the properties of one vertex beyond its position, such as normals or colors stored in
extra channels.
bitbybit.manifold.mesh.evaluate.transfor:
Reads the column-major 4x4 matrix that carries the original mesh onto one run of triangles,
the placement of that instance.
bitbybit.manifold.mesh.evaluate.numProp_: Counts the property channels each vertex of a mesh carries; the position alone takes three.
bitbybit.manifold.mesh.evaluate.numVert_:
Counts the property vertices of a mesh, which can exceed the geometric vertices where
neighboring triangles carry different properties.
bitbybit.manifold.mesh.evaluate.numTri_d: Counts the triangles of a mesh, which together make its whole surface.
bitbybit.manifold.mesh.evaluate.numRun_d:
Counts the triangle runs of a mesh: each run is a stretch of consecutive triangles that came
from the same instance of the same input shape.
bitbybit.logic.boolean_description:
Passes a boolean through unchanged, so a value can be given a name and reused.

Example: true -> true
bitbybit.logic.randomBooleans_descriptio:
Draws a list of random booleans, each true with a given probability.

Example: length 5 with trueThreshold 0.7 -> perhaps [true, true, false, true, true]
bitbybit.logic.twoThresholdRandomGradien:
Turns numbers into booleans with a random blend between two thresholds.

Below the first threshold a number is always true, above the second always false; in between,
the chance of true falls in steps from one to the other, so a pattern fades out instead of
switching sharply.
Example: [0.1, 0.9] with thresholds 0.3 and 0.7 -> [true, false]
bitbybit.logic.thresholdBooleanList_desc:
Turns numbers into booleans: true below the threshold, false at or above it.

`inverse` flips every result.
Example: [0.3, 0.7, 0.5] with threshold 0.6 -> [true, false, true]
bitbybit.logic.thresholdGapsBooleanList_:
Turns numbers into booleans: true when the number falls inside any of the given ranges, false
otherwise.

Each range is `[min, max]` with both ends included; `inverse` flips every result.
Example: [0.2, 0.5, 0.8] with ranges [[0.3, 0.6], [0.7, 0.9]] -> [false, true, true]
bitbybit.logic.not_description:
Flips a boolean: true becomes false and false becomes true.

Example: true -> false
bitbybit.logic.notList_description:
Flips every boolean in a list.

Example: [true, false, true] -> [false, true, false]
bitbybit.logic.compare_description:
Compares two values with an operator: less, less or equal, greater, greater or equal, equal
or not equal, in the loose (`==`) or strict (`===`) form.

Example: 5 greater than 3 -> true; 'hello' strictly equal to 'world' -> false
bitbybit.logic.valueGate_description:
Lets a value through when the boolean is true and gives undefined when it is false.

Example: 42 with true -> 42; 42 with false -> undefined
bitbybit.logic.firstDefinedValueGate_des:
Picks the first of two values that is defined, so the second acts as a fallback.

Example: 42 and 10 -> 42; undefined and 10 -> 10
bitbybit.math.number_description:
Passes a number through unchanged, so a value can be given a name and reused.

Example: 42 -> 42
bitbybit.math.twoNrOperation_description:
Applies one arithmetic operation to two numbers: add, subtract, multiply, divide, power or
modulus.

The operation reads `first` then `second`: subtract gives first minus second, power gives
first to the power of second.
Example: 5 add 3 -> 8, 10 modulus 3 -> 1, 2 power 3 -> 8
bitbybit.math.modulus_description:
Finds the remainder after dividing one number by another.

The sign follows the first number, as it does in JavaScript.
Example: 10 modulus 3 -> 1, 17 modulus 5 -> 2
bitbybit.math.roundToDecimals_descriptio:
Rounds a number to a given number of decimal places.

Example: 1.32156 to 3 places -> 1.322
bitbybit.math.oneNrOperation_description:
Applies one operation to a single number: absolute, negate, square root, rounding,
logarithms, the trigonometric functions and their inverses, exponential, or a conversion
between radians and degrees.

The trigonometric functions work in radians.
Example: sqrt of 5 -> 2.236, absolute of -3 -> 3
bitbybit.math.remap_description:
Maps a number from one range onto another, keeping its relative position.

A number outside the source range maps proportionally beyond the target range.
Example: 5 from [0,10] to [0,100] -> 50, 0.5 from [0,1] to [-10,10] -> 0
bitbybit.math.random_description:
Gives a random number from 0 up to, but not including, 1.

Example: 0.342, 0.891 or any other value in that range
bitbybit.math.randomNumber_description:
Gives a random number between `low` and `high`.

Example: low 0, high 10 -> 3.7, 8.2 or any other value between them
bitbybit.math.randomNumbers_description:
Gives a list of random numbers between `low` and `high`.

Example: low 0, high 10, count 3 -> [2.5, 7.1, 4.8]
bitbybit.math.pi_description:
Gives the constant pi, the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter.

Example: 3.141592653589793
bitbybit.math.toFixed_description:
Formats a number as text with a fixed number of decimal places, keeping trailing zeros.

Example: 3.14159 with 2 places -> '3.14', 5 with 3 places -> '5.000'
bitbybit.math.add_description:
Adds two numbers.

Example: 5 and 3 -> 8, -2 and 7 -> 5
bitbybit.math.subtract_description:
Subtracts the second number from the first.

Example: 10 and 3 -> 7, 5 and 8 -> -3
bitbybit.math.multiply_description:
Multiplies two numbers.

Example: 5 and 3 -> 15, -2 and 4 -> -8
bitbybit.math.divide_description:
Divides the first number by the second.

Dividing by 0 gives Infinity, as in JavaScript.
Example: 10 and 2 -> 5, 7 and 2 -> 3.5
bitbybit.math.power_description:
Raises the first number to the power of the second.

Example: 2 to the 3 -> 8, 5 to the 2 -> 25, 10 to the -1 -> 0.1
bitbybit.math.sqrt_description:
Finds the square root of a number.

A negative number gives NaN.
Example: 9 -> 3, 2 -> 1.414
bitbybit.math.abs_description:
Drops the sign of a number, so the result is never negative.

Example: -5 -> 5, 3 -> 3, 0 -> 0
bitbybit.math.round_description:
Rounds a number to the nearest whole number; halves round up.

Example: 3.7 -> 4, 2.3 -> 2, 5.5 -> 6
bitbybit.math.floor_description:
Rounds a number down to the whole number below it.

Example: 3.7 -> 3, -2.3 -> -3, 5 -> 5
bitbybit.math.ceil_description:
Rounds a number up to the whole number above it.

Example: 3.2 -> 4, -2.8 -> -2, 5 -> 5
bitbybit.math.negate_description:
Flips the sign of a number.

Example: 5 -> -5, -3 -> 3, 0 -> 0
bitbybit.math.ln_description:
Finds the natural logarithm of a number: the power e must be raised to for that number.

Example: 2.718 -> about 1, 1 -> 0
bitbybit.math.log10_description:
Finds the base-10 logarithm of a number: the power 10 must be raised to for that number.

Example: 100 -> 2, 1000 -> 3, 10 -> 1
bitbybit.math.tenPow_description:
Raises 10 to the power of a number.

Example: 2 -> 100, 3 -> 1000, -1 -> 0.1
bitbybit.math.sin_description:
Finds the sine of an angle given in radians.

Example: 0 -> 0, pi/2 -> 1
bitbybit.math.cos_description:
Finds the cosine of an angle given in radians.

Example: 0 -> 1, pi -> -1
bitbybit.math.tan_description:
Finds the tangent of an angle given in radians.

Example: 0 -> 0, pi/4 -> about 1
bitbybit.math.asin_description:
Finds the angle, in radians, whose sine is the given number.

Example: 0 -> 0, 1 -> pi/2 (about 1.57)
bitbybit.math.acos_description:
Finds the angle, in radians, whose cosine is the given number.

Example: 1 -> 0, -1 -> pi (about 3.14)
bitbybit.math.atan_description:
Finds the angle, in radians, whose tangent is the given number.

Example: 0 -> 0, 1 -> pi/4 (about 0.785)
bitbybit.math.exp_description:
Raises e, the base of the natural logarithm, to the power of a number.

Example: 0 -> 1, 1 -> about 2.718, 2 -> about 7.389
bitbybit.math.degToRad_description:
Converts an angle from degrees to radians.

Example: 180 -> pi (about 3.14159), 90 -> pi/2
bitbybit.math.radToDeg_description:
Converts an angle from radians to degrees.

Example: pi -> 180, pi/2 -> 90
bitbybit.math.ease_description:
Maps a value from 0 to 1 onto the range `min` to `max` along an easing curve, so the result
speeds up or slows down instead of changing evenly.

An `easeIn` curve starts slowly, an `easeOut` curve ends slowly, an `easeInOut` curve does
both.
Example: 0.5 from [0,100] with easeInQuad -> 25
bitbybit.lists.getItem_description:
Reads the item at a position in the list, counting from 0.

An index outside the list throws an error.
Example: [10, 20, 30, 40] at index 2 -> 30
bitbybit.lists.randomGetThreshold_descri:
Keeps each item of the list with a given probability and drops the rest, so the result
differs on every call.

Example: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] with threshold 0.5 -> perhaps [1, 3, 5]
bitbybit.lists.getSubList_description:
Cuts out the items from a start index up to, but not including, an end index.

Example: [10, 20, 30, 40, 50] from 1 to 4 -> [20, 30, 40]
bitbybit.lists.getNthItem_description:
Keeps every nth item, starting from an offset.

Example: [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8] with nth 3 and offset 0 -> [0, 3, 6]; with nth 2 and
offset 1 -> [1, 3, 5, 7]
bitbybit.lists.getByPattern_description:
Keeps the items where a repeating true/false pattern says true and drops the others.

The pattern starts over when it runs out.
Example: [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5] with pattern [true, true, false] -> [0, 1, 3, 4]
bitbybit.lists.mergeElementsOfLists_desc:
Regroups nested lists by position: the first items of every list go together, then the second
items, and so on.

`level` says how many levels of nesting to flatten inside each list first; 0 regroups them as
they are.
Example: [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]] at level 0 -> [[0, 3], [1, 4], [2, 5]]
bitbybit.lists.getLongestListLength_desc:
Measures the longest list among several.

Example: [[1, 2], [3, 4, 5, 6], [7]] -> 4
bitbybit.lists.reverse_description:
Reverses the order of the items.

Example: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] -> [5, 4, 3, 2, 1]
bitbybit.lists.flipLists_description:
Turns a list of lists on its side: rows become columns and columns become rows.

All the inner lists must have the same length.
Example: [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]] -> [[0, 3], [1, 4], [2, 5]]
bitbybit.lists.groupNth_description:
Splits the list into groups of n items.

Items left over at the end are dropped unless `keepRemainder` is on, which adds them as a
shorter last group.
Example: [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8] in groups of 3 -> [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5], [6, 7, 8]]
bitbybit.lists.getListDepth_description:
Measures how deeply lists are nested inside the list.

Example: [1, 2, 3] -> 1, [[1, 2], [3, 4]] -> 2, [[[1]]] -> 3
bitbybit.lists.listLength_description:
Counts the items in the list.

Example: [10, 20, 30, 40, 50] -> 5, [] -> 0
bitbybit.lists.addItemAtIndex_descriptio:
Inserts an item at a position; the items from that position on shift up by one.

Example: [10, 20, 30, 40] with 99 at index 2 -> [10, 20, 99, 30, 40]
bitbybit.lists.addItemAtIndexes_descript:
Inserts the same item at several positions of the original list.

Example: [10, 20, 30] with 99 at indexes [0, 2] -> [99, 10, 20, 99, 30]
bitbybit.lists.addItemsAtIndexes_descrip:
Inserts several items, the first at the first index, the second at the second, and so on, all
counted on the original list.

The indexes must be in ascending order and there must be one per item, or an error is thrown.
Example: [10, 20, 30] with items [88, 99] at indexes [1, 2] -> [10, 88, 20, 99, 30]
bitbybit.lists.removeItemAtIndex_descrip:
Removes the item at a position.

Example: [10, 20, 30, 40, 50] removing index 2 -> [10, 20, 40, 50]
bitbybit.lists.removeItemsAtIndexes_desc:
Removes the items at several positions, all counted on the original list.

Example: [10, 20, 30, 40, 50] removing indexes [1, 3] -> [10, 30, 50]
bitbybit.lists.removeAllItems_descriptio:
Empties the list it is given, in place: the same array comes back with no items in it.

Example: [10, 20, 30, 40] -> []
bitbybit.lists.removeNthItem_description:
Removes every nth item, starting from an offset.

Example: [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8] with nth 3 and offset 0 -> [1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8]
bitbybit.lists.randomRemoveThreshold_des:
Drops each item of the list with a given probability and keeps the rest, so the result
differs on every call.

Example: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] with threshold 0.5 -> perhaps [2, 4]
bitbybit.lists.removeDuplicateNumbers_de:
Removes repeated numbers, keeping the first occurrence of each.

Example: [1, 2, 3, 2, 4, 3, 5] -> [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
bitbybit.lists.removeDuplicateNumbersTol:
Removes numbers that are within a tolerance of one already kept, so values that differ only
by floating-point noise count as the same.

Example: [1.0, 1.001, 2.0, 2.002, 3.0] with tolerance 0.01 -> [1.0, 2.0, 3.0]
bitbybit.lists.addItem_description:
Adds an item at the end of the list.

Example: [10, 20, 30] adding 40 -> [10, 20, 30, 40]
bitbybit.lists.prependItem_description:
Adds an item at the start of the list.

Example: [10, 20, 30] prepending 5 -> [5, 10, 20, 30]
bitbybit.lists.addItemFirstLast_descript:
Adds an item at the start or at the end of the list, as chosen.

Example: [10, 20, 30] adding 5 first -> [5, 10, 20, 30]; last -> [10, 20, 30, 5]
bitbybit.lists.createEmptyList_descripti:
Makes a new list with nothing in it.

Example: -> []
bitbybit.lists.repeat_description:
Makes a list that holds the same item a number of times.

Example: 5 three times -> [5, 5, 5]
bitbybit.lists.repeatInPattern_descripti:
Repeats a pattern of items over and over until the list reaches a given length.

Example: [1, 2, 3] to length 7 -> [1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3, 1]
bitbybit.lists.sortNumber_description:
Sorts numbers from lowest to highest, or from highest to lowest.

Example: [5, 2, 8, 1, 9] ascending -> [1, 2, 5, 8, 9]; descending -> [9, 8, 5, 2, 1]
bitbybit.lists.sortTexts_description:
Sorts texts alphabetically, from A to Z or from Z to A.

Example: ['dog', 'apple', 'cat'] ascending -> ['apple', 'cat', 'dog']
bitbybit.lists.sortByPropValue_descripti:
Sorts objects by the number held in one of their properties.

Example: [{age: 30}, {age: 20}, {age: 25}] by 'age' ascending -> [{age: 20}, {age: 25}, {age:
30}]
bitbybit.color.hexColor_description:
Passes a hex color through unchanged, so a color can be given a name and reused.

Example: '#FF5733' -> '#FF5733'
bitbybit.color.rgbToHex_description:
Writes three channel values as a hex color.

`min` and `max` say which range the values use; a range other than 0 to 255 is remapped
first, so channels from 0 to 1 work as well.
Example: r 255, g 87, b 51 in [0,255] -> '#ff5733'; r 1, g 0.5, b 0.2 in [0,1] -> '#ff8033'
bitbybit.color.rgbObjToHex_description:
Writes an `{ r, g, b }` color as a hex color.

`min` and `max` say which range the channels use; a range other than 0 to 255 is remapped
first.
Example: { r: 1, g: 0.5, b: 0.2 } in [0,1] -> '#ff8033'
bitbybit.color.getRedParam_description:
Reads the red channel of a hex color, remapped to a range of your choice.

Example: '#FF5733' in [0,1] -> 1
bitbybit.color.getGreenParam_description:
Reads the green channel of a hex color, remapped to a range of your choice.

Example: '#FF5733' in [0,1] -> 0.341
bitbybit.color.getBlueParam_description:
Reads the blue channel of a hex color, remapped to a range of your choice.

Example: '#FF5733' in [0,1] -> 0.2
bitbybit.color.rgbToRed_description:
Reads the red channel of an `{ r, g, b }` color.

Example: { r: 255, g: 87, b: 51 } -> 255
bitbybit.color.rgbToGreen_description:
Reads the green channel of an `{ r, g, b }` color.

Example: { r: 255, g: 87, b: 51 } -> 87
bitbybit.color.rgbToBlue_description:
Reads the blue channel of an `{ r, g, b }` color.

Example: { r: 255, g: 87, b: 51 } -> 51
bitbybit.color.invert_description:
Inverts a hex color, turning each channel into its opposite: 255 minus the value.

With `blackAndWhite` on, the result is plain black for a light color or white for a dark
one, which suits text on a colored background.
Example: '#FF5733' -> '#00a8cc'; with blackAndWhite -> '#ffffff'
bitbybit.text.create_description:
Passes a text through unchanged, so a value can be given a name and reused.

Example: 'Hello World' -> 'Hello World'
bitbybit.text.split_description:
Cuts a text into pieces wherever a separator occurs; the separator itself is dropped.

Example: 'apple,banana,cherry' split by ',' -> ['apple', 'banana', 'cherry']
bitbybit.text.replaceAll_description:
Replaces every occurrence of a search text with another text.

Example: 'hello hello' replacing 'hello' with 'hi' -> 'hi hi'
bitbybit.text.join_description:
Joins a list of texts into one, with a separator between neighbors.

Example: ['apple', 'banana', 'cherry'] joined by ', ' -> 'apple, banana, cherry'
bitbybit.text.toString_description:
Turns any value into text, the way JavaScript prints it.

Example: 42 -> '42', [1, 2] -> '1,2'
bitbybit.text.toStringEach_description:
Turns every item of a list into text, the way JavaScript prints it.

Example: [1, 2.5, true] -> ['1', '2.5', 'true']
bitbybit.text.format_description:
Fills numbered placeholders in a text with values: `{0}` takes the first value, `{1}` the
second, and so on.

A placeholder without a value is left as it is.
Example: 'Point: ({0}, {1})' with [10, 5] -> 'Point: (10, 5)'
bitbybit.text.vectorChar_description:
Draws one character as line paths with a simple stroke font.

The paths lie flat on the XZ plane, scaled so the character is `height` tall, and are
returned with the character's width and height. An unknown character is drawn as a question
mark.
Example: 'A' at height 10 -> the strokes of an A, 10 units tall
bitbybit.text.vectorText_description:
Draws a text, with line breaks, as line paths with a simple stroke font.

Each line comes back as its characters with their paths, laid out flat on the XZ plane with
the given height, spacing and alignment; `centerOnOrigin` puts the middle of the block at the
origin.
Example: 'Hello' at height 10 -> five characters with their strokes
bitbybit.dates.toDateString_description:
Formats the date part as text, without the time, in the local time zone.

Example: 15 January 2024 at 14:30 -> 'Mon Jan 15 2024'
bitbybit.dates.toISOString_description:
Formats the date and time in the ISO 8601 form used for data exchange, always in UTC.

Example: 15 January 2024 at 14:30 -> '2024-01-15T14:30:45.000Z'
bitbybit.dates.toJSON_description:
Formats the date the way it appears inside JSON, which is the ISO 8601 form in UTC.

Example: 15 January 2024 at 14:30 -> '2024-01-15T14:30:00.000Z'
bitbybit.dates.toString_description:
Formats the full date and time as text in the local time zone, with the zone offset.

Example: 15 January 2024 at 14:30 -> 'Mon Jan 15 2024 14:30:00 GMT+0000'
bitbybit.dates.toTimeString_description:
Formats the time part as text, without the date, in the local time zone with the zone offset.

Example: 15 January 2024 at 14:30 -> '14:30:45 GMT+0000'
bitbybit.dates.toUTCString_description:
Formats the date and time as text in UTC.

Example: 15 January 2024 at 14:30 -> 'Mon, 15 Jan 2024 14:30:00 GMT'
bitbybit.dates.now_description: Gives the current date and time at the moment of the call.
bitbybit.dates.createDate_description:
Builds a date from its parts, read in the local time zone.

The month counts from 0: 0 is January, 11 December. A part outside its range rolls over, so
day 32 of January becomes the first of February.
Example: year 2024, month 0, day 15, hours 14, minutes 30 -> 15 January 2024 at 14:30 local
time
bitbybit.dates.createDateUTC_description:
Builds a date from its parts, read as UTC so the local time zone plays no part.

The month counts from 0: 0 is January, 11 December. A part outside its range rolls over.
Example: year 2024, month 0, day 15 -> 15 January 2024 at 00:00 UTC
bitbybit.dates.createFromUnixTimeStamp_d:
Builds a date from a Unix timestamp: the number of milliseconds since 1 January 1970 at 00:00
UTC.

Example: 1705329000000 -> 15 January 2024 at 14:30 UTC
bitbybit.dates.parseDate_description:
Reads a date written as text and gives its Unix timestamp, the milliseconds since 1 January
1970 at 00:00 UTC.

ISO 8601 text such as '2024-01-15' or '2024-01-15T14:30:00Z' is read reliably; text that
cannot be read gives NaN.
Example: '2024-01-15' -> 1705276800000
bitbybit.dates.getDayOfMonth_description:
Reads the day of the month, from 1 to 31, in the local time zone.

Example: 15 January 2024 -> 15
bitbybit.dates.getWeekday_description:
Reads the day of the week in the local time zone: 0 is Sunday, 6 Saturday.

Example: 15 January 2024 -> 1, a Monday
bitbybit.dates.getYear_description:
Reads the full year in the local time zone.

Example: 15 January 2024 -> 2024
bitbybit.dates.getMonth_description:
Reads the month in the local time zone, counting from 0: 0 is January, 11 December.

Example: 15 January 2024 -> 0
bitbybit.dates.getHours_description:
Reads the hour, from 0 to 23, in the local time zone.

Example: 14:30 -> 14
bitbybit.dates.getMinutes_description:
Reads the minutes, from 0 to 59, in the local time zone.

Example: 14:30 -> 30
bitbybit.dates.getSeconds_description:
Reads the seconds, from 0 to 59, in the local time zone.

Example: 14:30:45 -> 45
bitbybit.dates.getMilliseconds_descripti:
Reads the milliseconds, from 0 to 999, in the local time zone.

Example: 14:30:45.123 -> 123
bitbybit.dates.getTime_description:
Gives the date as a Unix timestamp: the milliseconds since 1 January 1970 at 00:00 UTC.

Example: 15 January 2024 at 14:30 UTC -> 1705329000000
bitbybit.dates.getUTCYear_description:
Reads the full year in UTC.

Example: 15 January 2024 -> 2024
bitbybit.dates.getUTCMonth_description:
Reads the month in UTC, counting from 0: 0 is January, 11 December.

Example: 15 January 2024 -> 0
bitbybit.dates.getUTCDay_description:
Reads the day of the month, from 1 to 31, in UTC.

Example: 15 January 2024 -> 15
bitbybit.dates.getUTCHours_description:
Reads the hour, from 0 to 23, in UTC.

Example: 14:00 UTC -> 14
bitbybit.dates.getUTCMinutes_description:
Reads the minutes, from 0 to 59, in UTC.

Example: 14:30 UTC -> 30
bitbybit.dates.getUTCSeconds_description:
Reads the seconds, from 0 to 59, in UTC.

Example: 14:30:45 UTC -> 45
bitbybit.dates.getUTCMilliseconds_descri:
Reads the milliseconds, from 0 to 999, in UTC.

Example: 14:30:45.123 UTC -> 123
bitbybit.dates.setYear_description:
Makes a copy of the date with another year, in the local time zone. The given date is not
changed.

Example: 15 January 2024 with year 2025 -> 15 January 2025
bitbybit.dates.setMonth_description:
Makes a copy of the date with another month, in the local time zone; months count from 0. The
given date is not changed.

Example: 15 January 2024 with month 5 -> 15 June 2024
bitbybit.dates.setDayOfMonth_description:
Makes a copy of the date with another day of the month, in the local time zone. The given
date is not changed.

Example: 15 January 2024 with day 20 -> 20 January 2024
bitbybit.dates.setHours_description:
Makes a copy of the date with another hour, in the local time zone. The given date is not
changed.

Example: 14:30 with hours 9 -> 09:30
bitbybit.dates.setMinutes_description:
Makes a copy of the date with other minutes, in the local time zone. The given date is not
changed.

Example: 14:30 with minutes 45 -> 14:45
bitbybit.dates.setSeconds_description:
Makes a copy of the date with other seconds, in the local time zone. The given date is not
changed.

Example: 14:30:00 with seconds 30 -> 14:30:30
bitbybit.dates.setMilliseconds_descripti:
Makes a copy of the date with other milliseconds, in the local time zone. The given date is
not changed.

Example: 14:30:00.000 with milliseconds 500 -> 14:30:00.500
bitbybit.dates.setTime_description:
Makes a copy of the date moved to a Unix timestamp, the milliseconds since 1 January 1970 at
00:00 UTC. The given date is not changed.

Example: any date with time 0 -> 1 January 1970 at 00:00 UTC
bitbybit.dates.setUTCYear_description:
Makes a copy of the date with another year, in UTC. The given date is not changed.

Example: 15 January 2024 with year 2025 -> 15 January 2025
bitbybit.dates.setUTCMonth_description:
Makes a copy of the date with another month, in UTC; months count from 0. The given date is
not changed.

Example: 15 January 2024 with month 5 -> 15 June 2024
bitbybit.dates.setUTCDay_description:
Makes a copy of the date with another day of the month, in UTC. The given date is not
changed.

Example: 15 January 2024 with day 20 -> 20 January 2024
bitbybit.dates.setUTCHours_description:
Makes a copy of the date with another hour, in UTC. The given date is not changed.

Example: 14:30 UTC with hours 9 -> 09:30 UTC
bitbybit.dates.setUTCMinutes_description:
Makes a copy of the date with other minutes, in UTC. The given date is not changed.

Example: 14:30 UTC with minutes 45 -> 14:45 UTC
bitbybit.dates.setUTCSeconds_description:
Makes a copy of the date with other seconds, in UTC. The given date is not changed.

Example: 14:30:00 UTC with seconds 30 -> 14:30:30 UTC
bitbybit.dates.setUTCMilliseconds_descri:
Makes a copy of the date with other milliseconds, in UTC. The given date is not changed.

Example: 14:30:00.000 UTC with milliseconds 500 -> 14:30:00.500 UTC
bitbybit.json.stringify_description:
Turns any JSON-compatible value into its JSON text, on one line without indentation, as
`JSON.stringify` does.
bitbybit.json.parse_description:
Turns JSON text into the value it describes, as `JSON.parse` does; text that is not valid
JSON throws an error.
bitbybit.json.query_description:
Finds every value in the JSON that a JSONPath expression matches and gives them as a list,
even when there is only one.

`$.parts[*].name` lists all part names and `$..radius` every radius at any depth; JSONPath
filters in square brackets narrow the matches by a condition.
bitbybit.json.setValueOnProp_description:
Sets one top-level property of a JSON object to a value, giving a changed copy; the input
stays as it is and a property that did not exist is added.
bitbybit.json.getJsonFromArrayByFirstPro: get json from array by first prop match
getJsonFromArrayByFirstPropMatch: get json from array by first prop match
bitbybit.json.getJsonFromArrayByFirstPro:
Finds the first object in a list whose property equals the given value, comparing with strict
equality, and gives it back; nothing matching gives undefined.

For anything beyond one property, use `query` with a filter.
bitbybit.json.getValueOnProp_description: Reads one top-level property of a JSON object; a missing property gives undefined.
bitbybit.json.setValue_description:
Sets property `prop` to `value` on every object a JSONPath expression reaches, giving a
changed copy of the JSON.

`path` points at the parent objects, `prop` names the property on them: `path: "$.parts[*]",
prop: "visible"` changes every part. A value that is not an object throws an error.
bitbybit.json.setValuesOnPaths_descripti:
Applies several `setValue` changes in one go: entry `i` of `paths`, `props` and `values` is
one change, applied in order to a copy of the JSON.
bitbybit.json.paths_description:
Lists the paths of every value a JSONPath expression matches, each as a full path from the
root such as `$['parts'][0]['name']`, instead of the values themselves.
bitbybit.json.createEmpty_description:
Gives a new empty object with no properties, a starting point for `setValueOnProp` and
`setValue`.
bitbybit.json.previewAndSaveJson_descrip:
Hands the JSON to the running application to show it and offer to save it as a file; the
application decides how the preview looks, and nothing happens when the value is empty.
bitbybit.json.previewJson_description:
Hands the JSON to the running application to show it; the application decides how the preview
looks, and nothing happens when the value is empty.
bitbybit.verb.curve.createCurveByKnotsCo: curve by knots control points weights
createCurveByKnotsControlPointsWeights: curve by knots control points weights
bitbybit.verb.curve.createCurveByKnotsCo: Creates a Nurbs curve by providing knots, control points & weights
bitbybit.verb.curve.createCurveByPoints_: Creates a Nurbs curve by providing control points
bitbybit.verb.curve.createBezierCurve_de: Creates a Bezier Nurbs curve by providing control points and weights
bitbybit.verb.curve.closestParam_descrip: Finds the closest param on the Nurbs curve from the point
bitbybit.verb.curve.closestParams_descri: Finds the closest params on the Nurbs curve from the points

bitbybit.tag.create_description:
Builds a tag description from its text, position, color, size and depth behavior, without
drawing it; `drawTag` or `drawTags` put it on screen.
bitbybit.time.registerRenderFunction_des:
Registers a function to run on every rendered frame, for animation; it receives the
milliseconds elapsed since the previous frame, so movement can be scaled by it.

The function stays registered until the scene is reset.
bitbybit.asset.getFile_description:
Loads a named asset of the running application as a File, through the lookup the application
supplies in `assetManager.getAsset`.

Which store the name is looked up in depends on the application; a missing asset rejects the
promise.
bitbybit.asset.getLocalFile_description:
Loads a named local asset, one kept in the browser rather than on a server, through the
lookup the application supplies in `assetManager.getLocalAsset`.

A name that resolves to several files gives a list.
bitbybit.asset.fetchBlob_description:
Downloads the content at a URL as a Blob, raw bytes without a file name; the server must
allow cross-origin requests.
bitbybit.asset.fetchFile_description:
Downloads the content at a URL as a File named after the last part of the URL, without its
query string; the server must allow cross-origin requests.
bitbybit.asset.fetchJSON_description:
Downloads the content at a URL and parses it as JSON; the server must allow cross-origin
requests and the body must be valid JSON.
bitbybit.asset.fetchText_description: Downloads the content at a URL as plain text; the server must allow cross-origin requests.
bitbybit.asset.createObjectURL_descripti:
Makes a temporary URL for a File or Blob held in memory, so it can be handed to anything that
loads from a URL, such as a texture or a model loader.

The URL lives as long as the page does.
bitbybit.asset.createObjectURLs_descript:
Makes a temporary URL for each File or Blob in a list, in the same order, as
`createObjectURL` does for one.
bitbybit.code.typeScriptEditor_descripti: Allows to write TypeScript code with full bitbybit intellisense in one function. Whatever start function returns it will be seen as an output of the component.
bitbybit.code.javaScriptEditor_descripti: Allows to write JavaScript code in one function. Whatever start function returns it will be seen as an output of the component.
bitbybit.code.jsonEditor_description: Allows to write JSON code. Whatever start function returns it will be seen as an output of the component.
bitbybit.flow.actions.keyboard_descripti: Will execute on keyboard events by clicking the buttons.
bitbybit.flow.actions.mouseClick_descrip: Will execute on mouse events by clicking the buttons.
bitbybit.flow.actions.start_description: Starts the control flow and triggers executions.
bitbybit.flow.actions.trigger_descriptio: Triggers the execution by clicking the button.
bitbybit.flow.babylon.gui.button_descrip: Will execute on various pointer events by clicking the left mouse button on babylonjs canvas.
bitbybit.flow.babylon.scene.pointerEvent: Will execute on various pointer events by clicking the left mouse button on babylonjs canvas.
bitbybit.flow.babylon.getEventDataFromOb: Gets event data from observed result of the observable listener.
bitbybit.flow.babylon.observableListener: Will subscribe and listen to any of the babylonjs observables.
bitbybit.flow.babylon.render_description: Executes on each babylonjs render frame.
bitbybit.flow.counters.counterMinMax_des: Counts the number of flow executions between min and max values. When max is reached it resets
bitbybit.flow.counters.counterSteps_desc: Counts the number of flow executions by starting on given count value and increasing at each execution by given step from the list, till steps are finished. When end is reached it resets
bitbybit.flow.counters.counter_descripti: Counts the number of flow executions.
bitbybit.flow.logic.booleanGateSilent_de: Triggers different execution events based on the value of boolean provided, but executes only when boolean changes its value, this prevents from multiple events firing constantly even though no change happened.
bitbybit.flow.logic.booleanGate_descript: Triggers different execution events based on the value of boolean provided.
bitbybit.flow.logic.flipFlop_description: Every time an event is executed a different event will fire, in essence creating a toggle functionality.
bitbybit.flow.logic.isUndefined_descript: Checks whether the value provided is undefined and triggers true or false event.
bitbybit.flow.loops.forEach_description: For each loop that walks through all the elements in the list.
bitbybit.flow.loops.for_description: For loop that executes body between two values.
bitbybit.flow.time.delay_description: Delays execution by given timeout in ms.
bitbybit.flow.time.interval_description: Executes the flow every given interval in ms.
bitbybit.lists.createList_description: Creates a list from the given elements.
bitbybit.lists.flatten_description: Flattens the list of lists into a single list.
bitbybit.lists.passThrough_description: Casts value to 'any' type and passes the input to output without any changes.
bitbybit.math.numberSlider_description: Creates a number with a slider. You can set up min, mac and step values.
bitbybit.consoleLog_description: Logs the input to the browser console.
bitbybit.previewData_description: Shows the input data in a preview overview area. It can be text, numbers, json objects, arrays, etc. Circular Javascript objects not allowed.
bitbybit.runner.getRunnerInputValue_desc: Get the runner input value from the inputs JSON. This component will always return an undefined value in the editor context.
bitbybit.runner.getRunnerInputs_descript: Get the runner inputs in JSON. This component will always return empty object in the editor context.
bitbybit.runner.setRunnerResult_descript: Sets the complete JSON result for the runner. Keep in mind that it is safer to set values as this method will overwrite the whole result object with the value provided.
bitbybit.runner.setRunnerResultArrayValu: Sets the runner result value on the proiperty of JSON object. Each value will be added to an array, that is the value of the property.
bitbybit.runner.setRunnerResultValue_des: Sets the runner result value on the proiperty of JSON object.
bitbybit.text.areaCreate_description: Creates a text area in the editor. You can set up the text, width and height of the area.
async context description: Create asynchronous context that can use await components, simplifying asynchronous code execution and readability.
await description: Waits for the promise to be resolved and returns the value.
catch description: Catches the error that may happen while running asynchronous code. User can choose to handle errors appropriately.
cancel the interval description: Cancels the interval execution by providing the handler.
cancel the timeout description: Cancels the timeout execution by providing the handler.
key down descritpion: Triggeres code when key down event happens.
key up description: Triggeres code when key up event happens.
key press description: Triggeres code when key press event happens.

block_validation_lower_or_equal: must be lower or equal to
block_validation_smaller_or_equal_than: must be smaller or equal than
block_validation_larger_or_equal_than: must be larger or equal than
save text to file description: Saves text to a file and allows you to choose the name and extension. This component does not preview the text and can be used in situations where text may be too big to edit in text area field.
print text on screen description: Prints text on screen. This component is useful for debugging purposes.
preview text and save to file: preview text and save to file
preview text and save to file descriptio: Prints text on screen and allows you to save it to a file. This component is useful for debugging purposes.
register render loop listener descriptio: Runs the statment in the render loop and indicates how much time has passed since last frame in timeElapsedFromPreviousFrame variable.
is key pressed description: Checks whether the key is pressed and returns true or false.
execute code after description: Executes the code after given timeout in seconds.
execute code every description: Executes the code every given interval in seconds.
